result:
I've planned round 235 as the last stage of SABA-B-11a and set `b-next.json` to **CONTINUE**. Round 234 passed C (18 rows, real browser, 0 bugs) and the gate published it as `c95b8a8`, which is the baseline for round 235. I didn't change any app source: `store/` is still at `c95b8a8` with a clean tree.

**Round 235: SABA-B-11a stage 2, the bars ruler becomes clickable.** This only applies when the project has a tempo; without one the bars ruler stays inert, exactly as today.
- **Top strip (upper 10 px):** a click starts playback from that point, snapped to the editing grid when Snap is on, with Alt to bypass. During playback it jumps there and keeps playing. This is Saba's decision 2, based on Live manual 6.1/6.3.
- **Lower part:** a click moves the playhead, the same as a click on the seconds ruler does today.
- **Drag and double-click:** drag scrolls or zooms, and double-click fits the project or zooms to the selection, as in Live 6.1.
- **Code:** the ruler's drag and click handling moves into a shared hook, `app/hooks/useRulerNavigation.ts`, which both rulers use. The strip gets a tooltip and a row in the `?` shortcut sheet, and no permanent text is added.
- **Scope and checks:** 8 granted files and 3 new ones; 1,087 tracked files are frozen, including all protected auth and purchase files. The task has 11 UI tests (BR1–BR10 plus BR4b), two mutants, and 20 browser rows for C at 1440×900 and 1280×720.

**Where I didn't follow the review: the seconds ruler keeps its click.** The approved review wanted it to scroll only, as in Live. But with no BPM the grid is in seconds (Saba's decision 3), so that would leave those projects with no ruler you can click to set the position. I sent this to Saba as a question rather than deciding it myself.

**Pre-checks on a scratch copy outside the repo:**
- Typecheck passed and lint was clean.
- Of the 107 related test files, 105 passed. The 2 failures are the test lists of string keys and shortcut rows, which the new string and sheet row must extend; the task grants those edits.
- I ran every browser recipe in Chromium against the current code and against the sketch, at both viewports, with 0 page errors.

**One open Medium, A-R234-REVIEW-M1.** When a project opens with a BPM clip already placed, the "tempo set from …" message is overwritten (tempo, grid and Snap are still correct). It can't happen in `/studio-lab` today because projects there always start empty, but the bug is real (A confirmed it in a test). I scheduled it as round 236, together with two small findings in the same code, before SABA-B-11b and before SRW-21 resumes. The fix needs permission to edit `ArrangementContext.tsx`, which is why it's a separate round.

**Questions for Saba:** five new ones are recorded as awaiting him:
- the seconds ruler's role;
- snapping the scrub jump to the editing grid instead of Live's quantization menu;
- hold-to-loop in the strip;
- right-click in the strip to add a locator;
- whether the three-sentence tempo message is too long.

SABA-B-7 (the envelope taper) and the tempo-undo question are still unanswered.

**Requests for root:**
- A non-blocking frontend-architect checkpoint, `b-round-234-checkpoint-request.md`, on the tempo/grid/Snap code in `StudioWorkspace.tsx`. It would help to run it before SABA-B-11b.
- My scratch dev server on port 5174 shared the untracked `node_modules/.vite` cache and re-optimised it once; no tracked file changed.

**Other notes:**
- Six smaller findings are recorded: five go to the deferred polish list and one is a note.
- The regression round isn't due until 2026-10-30.
- The advisor was available and I consulted it twice. Its final review found three gaps in the task text (the hook's folder, how the strip click is detected, the question count), and I fixed all three.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `current-task.md`
- `tasks/round-234.md`
- `b-round-234.md`
- `b-next.json`
- `backlog.json` (now v220)
